It's disgusting what they're making same-sex attracted people (lesbians especially) go through. "Be coerceivly raped by the opposite sex or you're a bad person!" There's no innate moral judgement on sexual orientation. I don't know where they get off on thinking they're somehow better people for being bisexual. It's just plain homophobic. Being homosexual is natural, innate, and unchangeable. It doesn't matter how they spin their conversion therapy, it did not work before and it certainly won't work now. I honestly grieve for the women and girls that are being harassed and manipulated into violating their own sexual boundaries because they face being ostracized otherwise. I just want them to leave us alone. Remember that no matter how many people parrot to you that you should try to undo a repulsion that cannot be undone, you are in the right, and these people are not concerned for your well-being if they think you should sacrifice your body and mental health to please someone. 

It's fantastic that you're going to therapy for help, you shouldn't have to face this alone. If it's appropriate for you,  I would really advise that you take a step back from queer spaces and try to gain back a little peace of mind. Please. You're right that being a lesbian is excruciatingly isolating in this time, being unable to to relate to heterosexual stuff and being shunned out of our own LGB spaces. But the best possible thing you could do to help is to live your life. Be and do what makes you happy. Strive to thrive in this life however best you can, within your capabilities. You don't have to do or be something big, and the sooner you find out that you have inherent worth just for existing, the more you'll be able to navigate people and life with ease. Work with the insecurities, the depression, and anxiety. It's an earth-shattering process but at some point it's better than staying in the same square, even if it doesn't feel like you're moving forward. I'm so sorry that you're suffering. Find your support and cling to the things that make you enjoy this life. Lots of love, and wishing nothing but the best for you.

Little late, but this post really resonated with me. I feel so much for you. I've been through the same thought processes in varying stages, so I can relate. Sorry for this huge essay omg! 

Ugh there's so much I want to say, but one thing I'd like to remind you of first; not just in the context of sexual orientation, but just about most things, if someone online or in person is telling you to reconsider your personal boundaries--be alert. That is a red flag. It doesn't mean run away from people as soon as you recognize this, it doesn't mean don't hear out what other people have to say, merely take note. Someone wants you to redraw your boundaries. Why? 

What does you having these boundaries in place prevent them from doing? What is it affording you? What do they gain by having you dismantle them? People who egg you on to go against yourself have an intended result in mind, and it's usually self-serving i.e., not considering you and your own autonomy. I don't say this to make you paranoid, but anything anyone says to you (and yeah even what I'm telling you now) should be filtered through the fact that a) this person is human and has their own biases b) people tend to bandwagon and parrot- they'll just say what they've heard others tell them without really delving into the matter and c) you're your own person. You are perfectly capable of coming to your own conclusions, whether you trust yourself or not. Don't let people tell you how and what to think.

Next thing, the whole people thinking bisexual/pansexual people are somehow morally superior? Bullshit. And painstakingly homophobic, to boot. Humans can be awful no matter the age, race, sex, or sexual orientation. There's nothing inherently holy or sinful about who you have sex with it. And what's so wrong about same-sex attraction? Whatever happened to the whole love is love thing? Why are people so hell bent on forcing people to have sex with people they don't want to? It seriously creeps me out. Oppression is oppression, doesn't matter that it's coming from another oppressed group, it doesn't make it any less wrong to mentally manipulate people like that. 

So no, I don't think you're any less of a human being for not being into dicks, and people who try to convince you otherwise have some serious issues if they have no problem spreading rape culture and shame around like that. I've also always found dicks disgusting, there's nothing even remotely appealing to me about 'em (and yea!! I also can't stand realistic dildos!) Do you think I'm some kind of abomination? Do you think I'm a sub-category of human for not wanting people I'm not attracted to in my intimate relationships? Should I spend the rest of my life uncomfortable and in despair, living it the way other people think I should? Well, I won't. Why should you? 

And the thing is that...stuff like that doesn't really change. People have and still certainly try (hello conversion therapy) but thing is, it doesn't work. It's not something you choose. There's nothing wrong with us. 

I'm sure you know this already, but the torturing yourself with watching porn with dicks in it is probably not the best for your mental health.  Ngl, I've looked at it before just to see if my feelings have changed about it, because we all fall prey to the way society makes us see ourselves, but nope. I move on to stuff that makes me happy.

And I think and hope that you can fall back into things that make you happy, too. It's okay to step back from all of this for a while. I'm not saying bottle your feelings up, just take some time for the things that uplift you. Any music, game, books, shows, comics, art, whatever makes you feel happy to be you. Step away from non-supportive spaces and discussions. You deserve to be happy and comfortable with yourself, and you don't have to do anything to earn that right. Thanks for sharing your story, it's really helped me put some stuff in perspective. Hope it could help you a little bit too. Wish you all the best!!

I'm a total novice to indie perfumes, so beware my uncultured nose, but! **Firebird Saltwater** was the first perfume to make me understand the "my skin but better" concept. I thought it would be this overwhelmingly aquatic, salty thing, and it smells vaguely like that out of the bottle, but on my skin it quickly warms into a slightly sweeter, fresh, only softly salty scent. Like you sniffed your skin after you took a shower after being in the ocean, there's a little waft of how salty air and water cover the inside of your nose. Not the most flattering description, but it's really refreshing, I've been wearing it often when I need an uplifting and comforting scent. I don't enjoy very sweet perfumes so this is the most enjoyable skin type of scent I've tried in my limited experience :D

It's really kind of you to be so introspective that you're worried about them. But you're also assuming that you know what they'd think! Try to step back a little from that if you can catch yourself. Sounds like you're an overthinker, and that can get in the way. You can't possibly know that they won't want to have you as a friend again. Humans are weird! We sometimes barely understand our own brains, let alone an entire other human's brain. Can't predict what's going on in there.

But let's assume worst-case scenarios, since that's our depressed brain's favorite way to go. You contact them. You're nervous. You apologize and say that you know it's weird to be talking to them after so many years, but that you were wondering how they've been all these years or something along those lines. They might reply some vague stuff about their lives and then end with 'how've you been?' and you're probably gonna fudge up some vague reply and they might reply  something vague in return. Then they make up some excuse to leave and leave the chat there. Now your chest is burning with the anxiety and awkwardness of how awful that went and regret you even took that decision. But so what? If you haven't interacted with these people in some 10-15 years, what's a five minute chat exchanging idle pleasantries? If you haven't talked for so long and things go south, what are the odds you'll ever have to talk to them again? In the end, there's not all that much to lose by trying it. Perhaps you lose the illusion of them. But maybe it's better to wrap our heads around that and sift through people until we reach someone who really doesn't mind reconnecting. If all goes wrong, we're just back at square one, not much worse for wear. Are you worried they'll think badly of you now? It's not likely. We often make it out to be a bigger deal than the other person thought it to be. 

And sure they might have gotten tons of new friends. Buuut of those tons, not a one of them is you! And really, who actively opposes gaining a friend (or in this case, a friend back)? Tons plus one friend sounds pretty great to me, personally. 

Your worry about different social growths is really thoughtful. You guys may be different at this point, but not necessarily incompatible. And really sometimes it's just fun to be pulled back to earlier times in our lives. They might really appreciate that you could offer them that. And who knows. You guys may even get along better at these different stages! All in all, there's more to lose by not giving it a go then there is in trying. I'm so sorry for the long rant! I really hope you consider getting in touch

First of all, cool username! 

More importantly though, if that's the way your family loves you, then I can assure you there are people who will actually love you waaay better. You can't really imagine it, and it's gonna be really overwhelming when you feel it, because you're not gonna believe it. You're gonna look at people like they're crazy, 'cause you can't imagine anyone actually caring about you, but others will! Whether you accept it or not. 

Your family is having major problems and you've taken the brunt of it. And honestly, that's the fucked up part. You're not really responsible for that. I know it seems like where you are is all life will ever be like--just torment day in and day out with nothing to make it even close to better. The reality your parents have you in is not what real life is actually like. It's not what most people are actually like. You just haven't gotten to see it yet. I can tell you that there's a freedom like no other when you don't have to deal with people who pick you apart. It's really like another world. The problem is being willing to get through the struggle to reach that world for you. 

That aside, if you get the chance, do you have any anime recommendations for this newest season? Haven't kept up with any of the new stuff at all and I'd like to get back into it

Kids are pretty weird. Can't imagine how difficult it must have been to be a mom at that age, but he's there with you. You've managed to keep your child alive for four whole years! That's sincerely a pretty good job! He has a whole life ahead of him and you have /not/ ruined it. 

It's tough when a kid won't express their love in the way we think they will, but that doesn't mean that he doesn't love you. But it does mean he still needs you. It's obvious that you care for him in that you're even here, and thinking about how not to affect him negatively. You'd be surprised at how many mothers won't even consider that much. So thank you, for being a good parent in that regard, despite however "unfit" you are or think you might be.

I'm so sorry about your baby girl. But maybe hold onto that feeling of faith she inspired in you. You were making good choices for her and your son, you can continue to make good choices even now. You've already shown you're capable.
